findings: The frozen context contains six source variants under one mechanism Canonical, including the scenario-selection variant. The candidate answers the shared CMS-versus-G1 comparison directly and includes version-aware selection guidance, so all six frozen source variants are covered without expanding into the adjacent CMS-only or G1-only Canonicals.

The CMS section matches the Oracle Java 8/9 packet: initial-mark and remark remain stop-the-world boundaries, most tracing/sweeping is concurrent, concurrent GC consumes application-visible CPU, floating garbage can survive to a later cycle, ordinary CMS collection does not compact, and concurrent mode failure is tied to space/freelist exhaustion before the concurrent cycle finishes.

The G1 section explains the required mechanism rather than only naming algorithms: Region organization, Collection Set selection, stop-the-world evacuation, compaction by copying, remembered sets/write barriers for cross-region references, and a history-based pause prediction model. It also preserves remembered-set/refinement CPU and memory cost instead of presenting Region-local collection as free.

Pause semantics are appropriately bounded. The candidate explicitly rejects both 'CMS is pause-free' and 'G1 is fully concurrent', and it treats MaxGCPauseMillis as a soft target rather than a hard real-time SLA.

Lifecycle facts are correctly version-scoped: G1 is default from JDK 9 onward, CMS was deprecated in JDK 9 and removed in JDK 14. The selection section therefore does not incorrectly present CMS as a current JDK 14+ deployment option.

The project-experience section does not fabricate production incidents, pause reductions, throughput gains or user history. It converts the source's scenario-selection request into an explicit same-workload validation plan for historical JDK 8 migration decisions.

The main non-blocking quality cost is oral density: the three-minute section is materially longer than literal three-minute delivery and the one-minute section is already at the maximum recommended five points. This lowers oral quality to 4/5 but does not create a hard failure or change the PASS decision.
